title: Shakuntala
hook: a baby left by a river in the forest, and birds standing guard around her

segments.voice: Yesterday, Damayanti and Nala face to face, mending a marriage with words both ways. Your line was Damayanti. Did you say one true sentence about something that needed mending? Day one thousand three hundred forty-nine.

A newborn lies alone on a riverbank in the forest. No mother nearby. No village. And around her, keeping off whatever might come out of the trees, are birds. That's how the Mahabharata's first book begins the life of Shakuntala, and it's a stranger start than the love story people remember. A king will come. Today we stay before the king arrives, with a girl, the birds, and the old hermit who heard her cry.
screen: `A NEWBORN ON A RIVERBANK.` → `BIRDS STANDING GUARD.` → `BEFORE THE KING ARRIVES.`

segments.voice: In the epic, Shakuntala tells her own beginning to a visitor, the way she heard it from the sage Kanva, who raised her. It starts with another sage, Vishvamitra, whose austerities are so fierce that Indra, king of the gods, grows afraid of his power. Indra sends the apsara Menaka, a celestial dancer, to break his concentration. She does. A daughter is born. Menaka leaves the baby beside a river in the forest and goes back to heaven. So the girl's parents are a great sage and a heavenly woman, and neither stays. Then the birds. The story says they gather around the baby and protect her in that lonely place. And Kanva, out for his bath, finds her. He brings her home to his hermitage and raises her as his daughter. He names her for the birds. The word for bird the epic uses is shakunta, and so she is Shakuntala, the one the birds protected. That's the epic's own explanation of her name. One more thing from Kanva. In the telling, he lists who counts as a father: the one who gives life, the one who saves a life, and the one who gives food. By that measure, he is fully her father. Sit with what that does to the romance ahead. Before she is anyone's beloved, Shakuntala is a child who was left, and then kept. Her name doesn't remember her famous parents. It remembers the small creatures who stood guard, and the old man who chose her. Whatever comes later in her story starts here, with a girl who knows exactly who took care of her.
screen: `VISHVAMITRA, MENAKA, AND A DAUGHTER` · `LEFT BY THE RIVER, GUARDED BY BIRDS` · `KANVA NAMES HER FOR THE BIRDS` · `LIFE, SAFETY AND FOOD MAKE A FATHER`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: whose bird are you? Settle, and let the breath slow. Kanva's three fathers were the one who gives life, the one who keeps a life safe, and the one who feeds it. Bring to mind someone you keep safe or feed right now: a child, a parent, a neighbor, a friend, an animal. Let them come into view on the in-breath. On the out-breath, picture yourself standing near them, the way the birds stood around the baby. Nothing to fix. Just stand guard for a few breaths. If you pray, you can hold them in prayer. The bell holds the time.
Shakuntala. The girl left by the river, guarded by birds, and named for them by the sage who raised her. Today's word.
Your line: Shakuntala. Today, feed or look after someone who isn't yours to look after, the way Kanva took in a child by the river. Day one thousand three hundred forty-nine.

howItsDone: Hindus know Shakuntala's story from the Mahabharata's first book, the Adi Parva, and from the poet Kalidasa's later play about her; her birth is told in both.

original.note: Sanskrit: the epic explains it from shakunta, bird: the one the birds protected.

trapdoor: what you thought: Shakuntala is the heroine of a love story.
what it means: before any king, she's a baby left by a river, guarded by birds, and raised by a sage who chose her.
what a scholar hears: the epic itself derives her name from shakunta, bird, and has Kanva define a father by life, safety and food.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva (Shakuntala tells her birth as Kanva told it: Vishvamitra's austerities; Indra sends Menaka; the baby left by the Malini river; the birds; Kanva finds and names her; Kanva's words on who is a father)

notes: The name: the Adi Parva has Kanva say he named her Shakuntala because she was protected by shakuntas (birds) in the forest. This is the text's own derivation, used under the claims rule; confirm.
Kanva's three kinds of father (the giver of the body, the saver of life, the giver of food): confirm the wording and that it appears in the Adi Parva telling.
Confirm Kanva found her while going to bathe (the epic places the baby by the river Malini). The river's name was left out of the voice.
